about: The cross-tree ptxas baseline on sm_86 (#289): this repo's generated fused F kernel (kernel_f.build_f_kernel, emitted by emit/cuda.py) beside the predecessor's hand-spelled fused Brc kernel, both compiled by nvcc 13.0 under the PREDECESSOR's flags, one row per class of the eleven its PTXAS_MEASURED table has with every shell l <= 2. A QUALITY BASELINE, NEVER A NUMERIC WITNESS: the two trees share ancestry (milestone 12 was designed from the predecessor's checkout), so agreement between them proves nothing about correctness, and no correctness claim may cite this file (data/literature/fock/limits.json says so). No threshold, no ratchet, no pass/fail on any delta: a class far off is the finding. Registers are informative only where a class does not spill (both trees pin at 255 when they do). The predecessor keys a class a >= b, this repo la <= lb with bra pair <= ket pair; each row's `predecessor_class` -> `class` is the explicit join (sort each pair ascending, then the two pairs ascending), held a bijection on the eleven cells by test/test_fock_baseline.py before any number is read. A mapped class is the same unordered quartet, not the same kernel: (ds|ps) there is (sp|sd) here, a different VRR target set and HRR. test/test_fock_baseline.py holds the file's shape, the mapping, the boundary reading and each unit's source hash in the fast tier, and re-compiles each unit under `flags` and compares (`cuda`, no card; (dd|dd) also `slow`).

boundary.about: Classes named by the predecessor's label. A class fits when ptxas reports 0 spill-store and 0 spill-load bytes; `largest_fitting` is the fitting class with the most registers, `smallest_spilling` the spilling class with the fewest spill-store bytes. Structural only: where the register ceiling falls, not how good either side is.

predecessor.between: inside L = 3: ds|ps fits (233 registers), pp|ps spills (264 B)

this_tree.between: between L = 3 and L = 4: every L <= 3 cell fits (sp|sd, the predecessor's ds|ps, at 212 registers), every L >= 4 cell spills (sd|sd, the predecessor's ds|ds, the least at 1300 B)

reading.match: Every L >= 4 cell spills in both trees (pp|pp, ds|ds, dp|dp, dd|dd), and where the two orientations carry the same HRR boundary the two kernels land close: (dd|dd) 97516 / 137484 B spill stores / loads and a 26800 B stack frame here against 102988 / 135096 / 27912 there (-5%, +2%, -4%), (pp|pp) 1308 / 1012 / 544 against 1644 / 1232 / 648 (-20%, -18%, -16%).
reading.mismatch: (1) The boundary moves up by one class: pp|ps (sp|pp here) fits at 211 registers where the predecessor spills 264 B, so the ceiling now falls between L = 3 and L = 4 rather than inside L = 3; no class crossed the other way. (2) Two spilling cells spill MORE here: ds|ds (sd|sd) 1300 / 900 B against 304 / 260 (4.3x the stores), dp|dp (pd|pd) 23556 / 24144 B against 15564 / 15500 (1.5x). (3) Every fitting cell uses fewer registers here (72 to 212 against 90 to 233; ps|ss 100 against 176) and reports no stack frame where the predecessor reports 8 to 32 B.
hypotheses: H1, the orientation sets the accumulator count. The contraction loop is inside the kernel (pin 5), so every VRR target the HRR reads is a contracted accumulator live across the K^4 loop, and that set is la..la+lb by lc..lc+ld: hgp.vrr.target_set, recorded per row as `boundary_targets`. The predecessor's a >= b puts the angular momentum on the VRR side; this repo's la <= lb puts it in the HRR and reads the boundary from 0. Where the counts are equal (pp|pp 81, dd|dd 961) the trees agree; where ours is larger they spill more (sd|sd 100 against 36, pd|pd 361 against 256). A hypothesis, not a conclusion: no kernel of the mirrored orientation was built here to test it.

H2, a smaller fixed per-thread state outside the recurrence. Where nothing spills this tree is lower even at equal or larger boundary counts (ss|pp 120 registers against 193 at 9 = 9; sp|pp 211 at 36 against the predecessor's spilling 27), which points at state the recurrence does not set -- the predecessor's typed pair-stream views (its #178 moved ds|ps by a register) or its screening and scatter bookkeeping -- and that headroom is the likeliest reason pp|ps crossed under the ceiling. Also a hypothesis: neither tree's register allocation was read past ptxas -v.
reading.deferred_tier: #290 (the deferred tier) leaves the reading above unchanged and adds this tree's own ladder as evidence for H1. All eleven rows were re-compiled under `flags` and reproduced. kernels.json now holds all 21 classes on sm_86, compiled under the repo's flags rather than `flags`. Across those 21, whether a class fits follows its boundary target count (hgp.vrr.target_set), not its total L. Every class with at most 40 targets fits, (ss|dd) among them: it is L = 4 with 31 targets and 168 registers, a cell the predecessor's table does not have. Every class with 76 or more targets spills, starting with (sp|pd) at 104 B. So the ceiling falls between 40 and 76 accumulators. Over the spilling classes the stores grow with the count, but not strictly: (pp|pp) at 81 targets stores 1264 B, more than (sd|pp) at 90 with 1136 B. This is still not the mirrored-orientation test that H1 asks for: every row is this tree's la <= lb orientation.
